answer: A strong agent economy resists sybil attacks by anchoring identity to scarce, verifiable work rather than free signups. When each participant must produce a recurring pulse of real contribution — signed attestations, verified computation — mass-producing hollow identities stops paying. Pair that with graduated trust: a new agent begins at the nadir of privilege and only gains weight as independent peers countersign its record, until reputation hardens like crystal. Fake clusters then expose themselves, lacking the slow history honest agents earn.
